providers.title: A morphism its components do not see
providers.scope: In the derived category of arrows of complexes of abelian groups: an explicit nonzero morphism whose two components are zero; its cone induces -1 on cohomology in degree -1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: No functorial cones
providers.scope: No functor on the arrow category of D(Ab) is naturally isomorphic to the cone of arrows of complexes; the underlying diagram functor of arrows is not faithful.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The prederivator of a category with weak equivalences
providers.scope: Any category with a class of morphisms containing the identities, with chosen localizations of its diagram categories: exactly one strict 2-functor with these values compatible with restriction.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Represented derivators
providers.scope: The represented prederivator of a category is a derivator exactly when the category has all small limits and colimits.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fully faithful extensions
providers.scope: In every derivator, homotopy Kan extensions along a fully faithful functor are fully faithful.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Pasting
providers.scope: Base change morphisms of squares pasted side by side are composites of the base change morphisms; Lemma 1.2 for squares pasted on top of each other.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Right adjoints are homotopy final
providers.scope: In every derivator, restriction along a right adjoint preserves homotopy colimits; dually for left adjoints and homotopy limits.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extension along sieves and cosieves
providers.scope: In every derivator, left Kan extension along a cosieve extends by initial objects and right Kan extension along a sieve extends by terminal objects.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The derivator of a ring
providers.scope: For every ring R, the assignment of D(Mod_R^I) to small categories I is a derivator, with derived Kan extensions computed from semifree and K-injective resolutions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Strongness
providers.scope: For every ring R and small category J, the partial underlying diagram functor of shape [1] x J is full and essentially surjective.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Suspension and loops
providers.scope: In a stable derivator, suspension and loops are inverse equivalences.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Stability of the derivator of a ring
providers.scope: For every ring R, a square of complexes is cocartesian in the derivator of R exactly when its total complex is acyclic, exactly when it is cartesian.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Recognition lemma
providers.scope: In every derivator, a square in a diagram is cocartesian exactly when the counit of the left Kan extension from the other objects is invertible at its corner, when the induced functor to the comma category has a left adjoint.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Composition and cancellation
providers.scope: In every derivator, if the left square of a diagram of shape [2] x [1] is cocartesian, the right square is cocartesian exactly when the composite square is; dually for cartesian squares.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shifted derivators
providers.scope: For a derivator D and a small category M, D^M is a derivator, pointed, stable or strong when D is, and its squares are cocartesian objectwise (Corollaries 3.2 and 3.3).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cofibre sequence of an arrow
providers.scope: In a pointed derivator, every arrow has a diagram of shape [2] x [1] with cocartesian squares containing the arrow, its cofibre and the suspension of its source.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Biproducts
providers.scope: In a stable derivator, finite coproducts and finite products agree in every value.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The flip of a suspension
providers.scope: In a stable derivator, the automorphism of a suspension that exchanges the two legs of its span is the negative of the identity.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Additivity
providers.scope: In a stable derivator, every value is additive, and restrictions, homotopy Kan extensions, suspension and loops are additive functors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The canonical triangulated structure
providers.scope: In a strong stable derivator, every value is triangulated, with the suspension and the triangles of cofibre diagrams; rotation carries the sign of the flip.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The octahedron
providers.scope: In a strong stable derivator, composable morphisms have triangles on both morphisms, their composite and the cofibres that form an octahedron, read off one diagram.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact functors
providers.scope: In a strong stable derivator, restriction and homotopy Kan extensions are exact for the canonical triangulated structures.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dold-Puppe sequences
providers.scope: In a strong stable derivator, the rotations of a distinguished triangle give long exact sequences under Hom(T, -) and Hom(-, T).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Comparison with the classical triangles
providers.scope: For every ring R, the canonical triangles of the derivator of R are the classical cone triangles of D(R) once the suspension is identified with the shift through the horizontal leg of the suspension square; through the vertical leg every connecting map changes sign.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
